policy_title: Improve Early Access to Mental Health Services
stated: Improve early access to mental health services by opening walk-in hubs for children and young people in every community and offering regular mental health check-ups at key points in people’s lives when they are most vulnerable to mental ill-health.

source.quote: Improve early access to mental health services by establishing mental health hubs for young people in every community and introducing regular mental health check-ups at key points in people’s lives when they are most vulnerable to mental ill-health. Improve early access to mental health services by: Opening walk-in hubs for children and young people in every community. Offering regular mental health check-ups at key points in people’s lives when they are most vulnerable to mental ill-health. Putting a dedicated, qualified mental health professional in every school, as set out in chapter 8.

bearing_set.reason: Directly expands mental health service access and capacity for children and adults at key life stages, affecting NHS waiting lists and mental health access indicators.

The policy specifically targets children and young people; poor and untreated mental health is a documented driver of school absence and attainment gaps, so expanded early access plausibly improves educational outcomes and reduces the attainment gap.

membership_note: Primary bearing is O3 (healthcare access, mental health specifically). O7 earns a real secondary bearing because the policy explicitly centres children and young people, and mental health is a well-evidenced barrier to school attendance and attainment. Other fundamentals (O12, O13, O14) are too indirect without funding detail or a pinnable indicator mechanism.
